The animation loops through five steps. Without animation every step shows at once.

g.text: a5: the amount of cos 5θ in p1
dashed: degrees 6 and 10, on top of it
a5 cos 5θ + b5 sin 5θ, set by the fit
order k of the Taylor term
at each point its tangent: the first derivative there
at this scale Δ and its tangents look straight
zoomed in: the straight line through the ends taken away
Δ bends by up to 6e-05, and the tangents turn
the slope changes along the line,
and its change is the second derivative
terms of the whole solution, all 769 numbers

which Newton corrects by about 10⁻³¹ in 3 steps
Below D 73 every harmonic can still be solved. Here is p1 at the centre over one echo period, at six of the 138.
Multiply the wave by cos 5θ and average over the period. Twice the average is a5, the amount of cos 5θ in the wave: one point against D.
3. Fit a polynomial through the points
A least-squares polynomial of degree 8 in 1/(D−2), times 1/√(D−2), passes within 10⁻¹² of all 138 points.
Past D 73 the polynomial gives the held value. At D 232.6 it sets the wave's harmonic-5 part. Fits of degree 6 and 10 differ by 3×10⁻⁹ there.
Δ looks straight, but zoomed in it bends. At a solved D the chain computes 24 derivatives of the whole solution; their Taylor sum predicts the next D.
